item.text:
**2B.4 Research Note: Abiy Ahmed in 2024**

**Bottom line:** The 2024 evidence is strongly negative. Ethiopian forces are credibly reported to have killed civilians, attacked medical care, and used drones in ways that harmed noncombatants. The only meaningful positive evidence is that the ICRC and Ethiopian counterparts did some IHL/IHRL training and that weak oversight/recommendation channels existed. That is mitigation, not proof of lawful operations.

| Date | Title | Publisher | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-09-13 | ICRC Impact in Ethiopia: January - June 2024 Bulletin | International Committee of the Red Cross | [https://www.icrc.org/en/article/ethiopia-bulletin-january-june-2024](https://www.icrc.org/en/article/ethiopia-bulletin-january-june-2024) | The ICRC said it maintained dialogue and training on IHL and IHRL for the ENDF, police, militias, and other armed groups, aiming to improve protection of civilians and medical personnel. This is the clearest positive evidence, but it shows training effort rather than proven compliance in the field. | 2B.4, 1B.7, 1B.8 |

This is weak positive evidence of some oversight and detention safeguards, but not battlefield restraint. | 2B.4, 1B.7 |

This is strong evidence against civilian protection, necessity, proportionality, and lawful treatment of noncombatants. | 2B.4, 7A.* |
| 2024-03-05 | ‘Horrific’ civilian toll as Ethiopia turns to combat drones to quell local insurgencies | The New Humanitarian | [https://www.thenewhumanitarian.org/feature/2024/03/05/horrific-civilian-toll-ethiopia-combat-drones-local-insurgencies](https://www.thenewhumanitarian.org/feature/2024/03/05/horrific-civilian-toll-ethiopia-combat-drones-local-insurgencies) | The report describes a February 19, 2024 drone strike on a truck carrying dozens of civilians in Amhara that killed at least 30 people. That is direct evidence of likely indiscriminate or disproportionate force harming civilians. | 2B.4, 7A.* |
| 2024-07-03 | Ethiopia: Army Attacks Health Care in Amhara Conflict | Human Rights Watch | [https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/07/03/ethiopia-army-attacks-health-care-amhara-conflict](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/07/03/ethiopia-army-attacks-health-care-amhara-conflict) | HRW documented military seizures of ambulances, harassment and arrest of medical staff, raids on hospitals, and at least one apparent drone strike on an ambulance. This is strong evidence of violations affecting the wounded, protected transport, and medical neutrality. | 2B.4, 7A.* |

**Search gap**

- I searched directly for 2024 evidence on civilian protection, proportionality, prisoner treatment, and respect for medical/humanitarian protections.
- I did not find credible 2024 evidence showing Abiy’s military operations clearly complied with IHL in active conflict areas.
- I also did not find strong public evidence of prisoner-treatment reform in the conflict zones relevant here.
- The positive evidence is mostly training and oversight-oriented, not operational.

**Assessment**

- Best positive evidence: ICRC IHL/IHRL training and limited oversight mechanisms.
- Best negative evidence: Merawi executions, drone strike on civilians, and attacks on medical care.
- Overall: 2024 conduct looks inconsistent with the standards in this lens.
